Grecia
grē´shĭ-ȧ
n. (Greece; in Daniel the third of the four kingdoms, named centuries before it rose)
Latin Graecia. The KJV uses Grecia for the Hebrew and Aramaic Yavan, Javan, the son of Japheth whose descendants settled the Aegean.

Biblical Definition

Daniel is given the interpretation outright: “the rough goat is the king of Grecia: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king” (Dan 8:21), and the sequel — “that being broken, whereas four stood up for it, four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not in his power” (Dan 8:22). The angel names it as a power still to come: “the prince of Grecia shall come” (Dan 10:20). And chapter eleven begins the detailed account: “there shall stand up yet three kings in Persia; and the fourth… shall stir up all against the realm of Grecia” (Dan 11:2). The scheme was set in chapter two: “another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth” (Dan 2:39).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a kingdom as the territory or country subject to a king, and prophecy as a foretelling; prediction; a declaration of something to come.

expand to see more

KINGDOM, n. The territory or country subject to a king; an undivided territory under the dominion of a king or monarch.

PROPHECY, n. A foretelling; prediction; a declaration of something to come. As God only knows future events with certainty, no being but God can utter a real prophecy.

MONARCHY, n. A state or government in which the supreme power is lodged in the hands of a single person.

Key Scripture

Dan 2:39 — "And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee, and another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth."

Dan 8:21 — "And the rough goat is the king of Grecia: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king."

Dan 8:22 — "Now that being broken, whereas four stood up for it, four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not in his power."

Dan 11:2 — "And now will I shew thee the truth. Behold, there shall stand up yet three kings in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than they all: and by his strength through his riches he shall stir up all against the realm of Grecia."

Modern Corruption

Daniel names Grecia and describes the break-up of its empire into four while Babylon still stood and Persia had not yet fallen.

expand to see more

Daniel 8:21-22 is precise enough to be embarrassing to unbelief. The rough goat is the king of Grecia; the great horn is the first king; that horn is broken at the height of its strength and four kingdoms stand up in its place, but not in his power. Alexander died at thirty-two and his empire was divided among four of his generals. Daniel wrote in the sixth century, in the reign of Belshazzar, with Babylon still standing. Chapter 2 had already laid the frame — gold, silver, brass, iron — and the stone cut without hands that breaks them all and fills the whole earth.

The corruption to name is the late-dating of Daniel, which the critical schools have maintained since Porphyry in the third century for one stated reason: prophecy this specific must have been written after the events. The argument is circular and its premise is theological rather than historical — it assumes what it claims to prove, that God does not foretell. Christ settled the authorship for the church by citing Daniel the prophet in the Olivet Discourse. Daniel 11:2 begins, now will I shew thee the truth, and the God who says that is the God who declares the end from the beginning.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Yavan (H3120), Javan, Greece; Aramaic malku (H4437), kingdom; tsaphir (H6842), he goat.

expand to see more

Hebrew Yavan (H3120) — Javan, Grecia; Daniel 8:21, 10:20, 11:2, Genesis 10:2.

Aramaic malku (H4437) — kingdom, reign; Daniel 2:39, 2:44.

Hebrew tsaphir (H6842) — he goat; Daniel 8:21, 8:5.

Hebrew qeren (H7161) — horn, power; Daniel 8:21, 8:22, Psalm 75:10.

Aramaic nechash (H5174) — brass; Daniel 2:39, 2:32.

Usage

"“The rough goat is the king of Grecia” — named before it rose."

"“Four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not in his power.”"

"“A third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth.”"
